entries.description: It’s easier to enter the world starting with boundaries, rhythms, instinctive judgements, and “what’s not right”.
entries.strength_expression: In scenes that require realistic actions, rhythms, and boundaries, this set of clues may help you notice earlier where closure, protection, or adjustment is needed; whether it is effective still depends on information, authorization, and relationship conditions.
entries.cost_expression: When physical discomfort accumulates, you may first respond by stiffening up, tightening your grip, or increasing your sense of control; this is more likely to be viewed as a stress cue than a character flaw.
entries.stress_signal: Start to tense up, rush to correct the deviation, push directly or press yourself very hard.
entries.observation_question: What did you feel first today was something wrong in your body, or was it the explanations and reasoning in your mind?
entries.boundary_note: Center groups are the explanatory framework within the Enneagram theory and can only help to observe where attention may fall first; the current results page does not confirm your center type, emotional mechanism or physical and mental state.
entries.availability_note: This module first displays theoretical boundaries and observation questions, and does not directly convert the current answers into central scores or central judgments.

entries.description: It is easier to understand oneself and others from the perspective of value, relationship position, being seen, and emotional atmosphere.
entries.strength_expression: In scenarios where you need to take care of relationship temperature, feedback, and identity cues, this set of cues may help you notice changes in responses more quickly; it does not mean you can always accurately read people or the nature of the relationship.
entries.cost_expression: When relational responsiveness, recognition, or a sense of difference is important, feelings of self-worth may be more easily affected by external feedback; this suggests the need to view feedback and personal value separately.
entries.stress_signal: Begin to compare excessively, care too much about relationship status, or tie emotional experience and sense of value too tightly.
entries.observation_question: What do you care most about today, is whether things are accomplished or how you are seen?
entries.boundary_note: Center Groups are an explanatory framework within the Enneagram Theory and can only help to see where attention may land first; the current results page does not confirm your center type, emotional mechanism, or relationship value.
entries.availability_note: This module first displays theoretical boundaries and observation questions, and does not directly convert the current answers into central scores or central judgments.

entries.description: It is easier to process reality starting from understanding, anticipation, possibility, security and space for choice.
entries.strength_expression: In scenarios where information, risks, and paths need to be sorted out, this set of clues may help you discover structures and information gaps; it does not mean that judgment is necessarily more objective, and it also requires calibration with realistic feedback.
entries.cost_expression: When thinking, rehearsal, or option management continues to be prolonged, real entry and commitment may be delayed; this prompts the need to set stopping conditions and reality check points.
entries.stress_signal: Start over-rehearsing, keep options open, delay entering the market, or replace experience with ideas.
entries.observation_question: Is your judgment today helping you take action, or is it delaying your entry into real-life interactions?
entries.boundary_note: Center clusters are an explanatory framework within the Enneagram theory and can only help to see where attention might land first; the current results page does not confirm your center type, anxiety level, or cognitive abilities.
entries.availability_note: This module first displays theoretical boundaries and observation questions, and does not directly convert the current answers into central scores or central judgments.

entries.description: In the Enneagram stance theory, the assertive group is often used to describe a tendency to push outward faster, occupy space, or pull the rhythm. It can only be used as a situational observation clue and cannot indicate that you are active, strong or outgoing in all situations.
entries.strength_expression: When the goal is clear, the situation is stagnant, or someone needs to take the lead, this set of clues may help you drive the pace, bear the cost of advancement, and push the next step forward; you still need to check other people's resources and true authorization.
entries.cost_expression: If pushing becomes a habitual response, fatigue, limitations, loss, or relationship costs may be seen later; review should return to the specific event rather than treating it as a fixed flaw.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include faster tempo, increased intensity, harder pauses, or putting aside vulnerabilities and limitations.
entries.observation_question: When you take the initiative today, are you actually protecting goals, relationships, boundaries, or feelings of uncertainty? Is there a scene where you were able to stop and pace yourself as well?
entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a behavioral style measure, extraversion judgment, leadership rating, or stable personality classification.

entries.description: In Enneagram stance, the compliant group is often used to describe a tendency to act with reference to responsibilities, rules, relationship obligations, or trustworthy standards. It can only be used as a situational observation clue, but it does not mean that you are always submissive, ingratiating, or lacking in assertiveness.
entries.strength_expression: When a promise needs to be fulfilled, a rule needs to be seen, or a relationship needs someone to take responsibility for, this set of clues may help you put responsibility into specific actions; it does not mean that you have to bear the consequences for everyone.
entries.cost_expression: If the sense of responsibility becomes a habitual reaction, "I agree" and "I should" may be mixed up, and the true needs will be expressed later; this requires calibrating the responsibility boundary with specific events.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include taking too much responsibility, double-checking, taking too much care of others, or having a hard time shutting down your inner “shoulds.”
entries.observation_question: When you take on something today, does it actually come from recognition, relationship responsibility, risk prediction, or fear of disappointing people? Is there a scenario where you could also clearly say no or renegotiate?
entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a compliance measure, moral evaluation, relationship diagnosis, or stable personality classification.

entries.description: In Enneagram theory, the withdrawn group is often used to describe a tendency to turn inward to organize feelings, energy, understanding, or rhythm before deciding when to enter the scene. It can only be used as a situational observation clue, but it cannot mean that you are always avoiding, being cold, or lacking in action.
entries.strength_expression: When information is overloaded, emotions need to be settled, or the pace of the scene is too fast, this set of clues may help you retain space and organize internal clues; if there is a lack of action to return to the scene, it may also be misinterpreted as exiting.
entries.cost_expression: If holding space becomes a habitual reaction, the action of returning to the scene may become delayed, and observation, numbness, or self-world may temporarily replace real action; this needs to be checked with specific situations.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include being quieter, more withdrawn, more procrastinating, or having difficulty bringing stance and needs back to real interactions.
entries.observation_question: When you step back today, are you actually restoring energy, organizing information, protecting relationships, or avoiding conflict? Is there a scene where you were able to re-enter and take a stand as well?
entries.boundary_note: Stance is a theoretical grouping, not a measure of avoidance, an assessment of sociability, a clinical judgment, or a stable personality classification.

entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the positive outlook group is often used to observe whether people tend to ease the situation, reconstruct meaning, lighten the atmosphere, or find an exit when faced with disappointment, friction, or pressure. It is not a measure of optimism, nor does it indicate that you avoid problems.
entries.strength_expression: When you are under short-term pressure, the team atmosphere is sinking, or the relationship needs to be stabilized first, this set of clues may help you retain hope, reduce the sense of collapse, and gain space for subsequent processing; it is not proof of avoiding the problem.
entries.cost_expression: If de-escalation becomes an inertial response, problems may be dismissed prematurely and real losses, boundaries or conflict issues postponed; this requires going back to the specific incident for verification.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include rushing to turn the page, convincing yourself that it’s okay, or hiding the real costs with kindness, optimism, changing the subject, and following along.
entries.observation_question: When you say "nothing" or try to lighten the mood today, are you actually restoring flexibility, protecting relationships, or letting important issues go out of sight for the time being?
entries.boundary_note: Harmonics are stress coping cues, not emotion regulation ability scores, mental health judgments, moral evaluations, or stable personality classifications.

entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the competency group is often used to observe whether people tend to use standards, efficiency, structures, or executable steps to bring the situation back to order when faced with problems, pressure, or a sense of loss of control. It is not a measure of ability, nor does it indicate that you are always rational or apathetic.
entries.strength_expression: When there is confusion, information is scattered, or responsibilities need to be implemented, this set of clues may help you organize the problem, break it down into tasks, and make the next step executable; the conclusion still needs to be tested by the situation and feedback from others.
entries.cost_expression: If dealing with problems becomes a habitual reaction, emotional and relationship costs may be skipped, and human problems may be prematurely technicalized; when reviewing, you need to look at who was affected at the time.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include cold expressions, increased speed, an overemphasis on the right thing to do, or acting like you are fixing the system rather than confronting the person who is being affected.
entries.observation_question: When you turn problems into tasks today, are you actually restoring order and preventing loss of control, or are you avoiding the cost that people and relationships are suffering?
entries.boundary_note: Harmonic is a stress response cue, not an evaluation of ability, a rating of rationality, a judgment of emotional maturity, or a classification of stable personality.

entries.description: In the Enneagram harmonic theory, the reactive group is often used to observe whether people tend to express tension first in situations that are unreal, unstable, unfair, or threatening. It’s not an emotional label, nor does it mean you’re always impulsive or difficult.
entries.strength_expression: When issues are suppressed, risks are downplayed, or boundaries are violated, this set of cues may help you let the cracks surface and resist pretending that nothing is wrong; the intensity of expression still needs to serve fact-checking and repair.
entries.cost_expression: If a strong reaction becomes a habitual reaction, the power of expression may be seen first, but the real need, worry or injury point is covered up; this requires going back to the trigger point for review.
entries.stress_signal: Observable signs of stress include being quicker to react, quicker to defend or test others, and more difficult to distinguish between expressing a need or protecting a wound first.
entries.observation_question: What is your strong reaction actually protecting today: truth, fairness, safety, boundaries, or some more sensitive point of hurt?
entries.boundary_note: Harmonic is a stress coping cue, not a mood stability diagnosis, impulsivity measure, relationship risk label, or stable personality classification.
